content: Indoor Asset Detection in Large Scale 360Â° Drone-Captured Imagery via 3D Gaussian Splatting | EECS at UC Berkeley Indoor Asset Detection in Large Scale 360Â° Drone-Captured Imagery via 3D Gaussian Splatting Monica Tang EECS Department, University of California, Berkeley Technical Report No. UCB/EECS-2026-1 January 5, 2026 http://www2.eecs.berkeley.edu/Pubs/TechRpts/2026/EECS-2026-1.pdf 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) is a powerful reconstruction method that enables high-quality, photorealistic novel-view synthesis from a collection of 2D images. Building on prior work that reconstructs indoor environments in 3DGS using 360 drone-captured imagery, we present an approach for object-level detection and segmentation of target indoor assets in 3DGS scenes. Existing methods for 3DGS segmentation leverage 2D segmentation masks per viewpoint. A fundamental challenge in this paradigm is the lack of multi-view consistency in mask IDs, whereby the same physical object is assigned different IDs across views. Prior approaches address this issue using video-tracking or 3D-aware memory banks; however, these strategies struggle for multi-video-stream imagery of large, object-dense indoor environments, often leading to erroneous object merges or inconsistent object representations across views. To address these limitations, we propose a 3D object codebook that jointly leverages the semantic labels of masks and the spatial information of their corresponding Gaussian primitives to guide mask association and indoor asset detection. Our method integrates 2D object detection and segmentation models to identify target objects in individual images, followed by semantically- and spatially-constrained merging procedures that aggregate masks from multiple views into coherent 3D object instances. We further introduce confidence-based and spatial filtering strategies to refine object geometry and suppress spurious object-Gaussian associations. Experimental results on two large indoor scenes demonstrate that our approach achieves reliable multi-view mask consistency, yielding 65% improvement in F1 score over state-of-the-art baselines, as well as accurate object-level 3D indoor asset detection, with an 11% improvement of mAP compared to baseline methods.
